Tooltip_craft_saltingTubDesc: Presses up to 50 weight of salt-packed fish under a weighted board for 1 to 2 days, longer for bigger fish. Nothing more goes in until the pressed fish is taken out.
Tooltip_craft_dryingFrameDesc: Hangs up to 8 stacks of fish, up to 2.5 weight each, in the open air for 12 to 30 days. Salt Pressed fish dries fastest in warm, dry weather. Gutted fish needs a cold season, or it spoils. Rain stops the drying.
Tooltip_craft_dryingBeamMediumDesc: Hangs up to 4 stacks of fish, up to 15 weight each, on hooks. Dries like a Fish Drying Frame, for fish too big to hang on one. Open air or under an open roof, not in a room.
Tooltip_craft_dryingBeamLargeDesc: Hangs up to 2 stacks of fish, up to 50 weight each, on hooks. Dries like a Fish Drying Frame, for the biggest fish. Open air or under an open roof, not in a room.
Tooltip_craft_hangFishToDry: Salt drying, for Salt Pressed fish. Works in any season, fastest in warm, dry air, best in the shade. Keeps for months.
Tooltip_craft_hangFishToColdDry: Cold drying, for gutted fish and halves. Needs a cold season, out of a room, or the fish rots. Keeps for a year or more.
Tooltip_TraditionalPreservationFishMeat_: Takes 4 salt for each started half weight of the packed fish, about a seventh of its weight. Carry the salt yourself: a shaker holds 10, a Bag of Salt 50. A fish over 4.5 weight is too thick to salt whole: gut and split it first.
Press it in a Salting Tub before it spoils.
Cured, but not yet preserved. Rinse off the salt if you like (right-click), then hang it on a Fish Drying Frame.
Hang it on a Fish Drying Frame in a cold season, or cook it. Split it if it's too heavy to hang.
Hang it on a Fish Drying Frame in a cold season, or cook it.

Raw, it will make you sick. Cook it, or add it to a soup or stew. It can't be dried. It also makes chum.
Fish head stock, ready to take up to 6 stew ingredients and your seasonings. It starts out as tasty as a plain stew. Cook it before eating.
Tooltip_craft_rinseSaltedFish: Optional. Soaks the excess salt off before hanging, as on the Volga. The dried fish is less salty (less thirst, no sour note) but keeps a tenth less long. Near a sink, bathtub, barrel or well, right-click the fish for Rinse at Sink.
Tooltip_TraditionalPreservationFishMeat_: Rinses %1 fish with %2 L of clean water from the sink, bathtub, barrel or well close by. The dried fish is less salty but keeps a tenth less long.
Tooltip_craft_stockfishPalletDesc: Where stockfish ripens, stacked as in the old warehouses. Cold Dried fish on it ripens twice as fast in a loft (a room upstairs) and half as fast again in a ground-floor room; covered, outdoors or in a damp basement, no faster than a shelf. Holds 20 weight.
Tooltip_TraditionalPreservationFishMeat_: Stockfish tied up as it was shipped from the Lofoten. Holds 10 weight of stockfish and nothing else; the fish ripen inside, on a pallet too.
Ties %1 stockfish (%2 weight) into a bale with %3. A bale holds 10 weight; the rest stay out.
Needs Twine or a Rope.
The fish go into your inventory and you get back the %1.
